Order 
This arbitration appeal has been filed under Section 37(1)(C) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act against order dated 21/01/2022 passed by IV th District Judge, Shivpuri in MGC AV No.01/2020 by which award dated 03/04/2017 passed by Arbitrator cum Divisional Commissioner, Gwalior Division, Gwalior in case No.181/15-16/R.R. MARG has been set aside.
2. I.A.No.3554/2023 has been filed under Section 5 of read with Section 14 of Limitation Act.

3. Considered the question of condonation of delay.
4.

This application reads as under:-
"APPLICATION U/S 5 R/W SECTION.14OF LIMITATION ACT FOR CONDONATION OF DELAY MAY IT PLEASE THIS HON'BLE COURT.

The humble appellant submits as under: -

sentences.text:
That, present Arbitration appeal has been filed by appellants against order dt.
21/01/2022 passed by court below under section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
The facts mentioned in the memo of appeal may also kindly be taken into consideration while deciding present application.
In filing of the present appeal, as per office report there is a delay of 348 days.
2. That, due to setting aside of arbitral award, Appellants kept waiting that appropriate proceeding would be initiated as per procedure established by law.

However bonafidely process was filed before collector and same was decided through order dated 24-03-2023 thereafter finding no way present petition is being filed before Hon'ble high Court as no proceedings were initiated by the Arbitrator.

3. That, time taken to participate before Arbitrator was based on bonafide belief that as per statute District collector is required to pass order for enhancement and appropriate compensation, hence delay passed in proceedings before Collector Shivpuri may kindly be condone as per section 14 of Limitation Act.
Delay being bonafide may kindly be condoned.

Prayer:
It is, therefore respectfully prayed that application for condonation of delay may kindly be allowed and while condoning the delay, appellants may kindly be permitted to continue with the Arbitration Appeal on merits in the interest of justice."
5.
Before considering the application, this Court would like to refer certain facts which are necessary for disposal of this appeal.
On 04/11/2012, a notification was issued for acquisition of land, and accordingly, 0.265 hectares of land belonging to appellant was acquired and total amount of Rs.1,97,785/- was paid.

The appellant filed his objection before the competent authority on 17/11/2012 with regard to the quantum of compensation and accordingly, the Arbitrator cum Divisional Commissioner, Gwalior by award dated 18/02/2020 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:31813 3 AA-220-2023 maintained the award against which an application under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act was filed by appellant before IVth District Judge,
Shivpuri.

6. By order dated 21/01/2022 passed by IVth District Judge, Shivpuri in MGC AV No.01/2020, the award passed by Arbitrator cum Divisional Commissioner was set aside, thereafter, appellant did not take any action.

It appears that after the record of Arbitrator cum Divisional Commissioner,
Gwalior was returned back, Divisional Commissioner, Gwalior suo moto restarted the proceedings and in the year 2022 on account of amendment by which District Collectors of their respective districts where the property is situated were made the Arbitrator, Commissioner forwarded the matter to the Collector, Shivpuri.
Collector, Shivpuri by order dated 24/03/2023 dismissed the reference.

It is submitted that since the appellant as bonafidely prosecuting his cause, therefore, the time spent by appellant before Commissioner, Gwalior as well as Collector, Shivpuri is liable to be excluded.

sentences.text: 7. Considered the aforesaid submissions made by counsel for the appellant.

8. This Court by judgment dated 25.07.2025 passed in A.A. No.37/2022 [The National Highways Authority of India (Ministry of Road Transport and Highways) Govt. of India Vs. Sanjay Kumar and Others] has held that since the Divisional Commissioner, Gwalior was the Arbitrator, therefore, the competent Court under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act would be District Court,
Gwalior and not District Court, Shivpuri, and therefore, order passed by IVth District Judge,
Shivpuri in identical cases were set aside with a direction to return the application filed under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act for presentation of the same before the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31813 4 AA-220-2023 competent Court.

entities.text: National Highways Authority of India (Ministry of Road Transport and Highways) Govt. of India Vs. Sanjay Kumar and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Although in some of the cases in which the aforesaid order has been passed were argued by counsel for appellant himself,
and he is also aware of the aforesaid fact, but surprisingly, he did not take the defence of lack of jurisdiction of the Court of IVth District Judge, Shivpuri.

entities.text: Court of IVth District Judge, Shivpuri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This aspect was specifically pointed out to Shri Sunil Jain that once, it has already been held that IVth District Judge, Shivpuri was not having jurisdiction to entertain an application against an award passed by Commissioner, Gwalior ,
therefore, his judgment is a nullity in spite of that Shri Sunil Jain did not argue that the original award dated 21/01/2022 be set aside on the ground of lack of jurisdiction and matter may be remanded back to District Court, Gwalior for adjudication.
9.
On the contrary, it was submitted by Shri Jain that he does not wish to challenge the award dated 21/01/2022 passed by IVth District Judge, Shivpuri on the ground of lack of jurisdiction.

Although,
it is well established principle of law that if any findings have been recorded by a Court having no jurisdiction, then such findings would be nullity, but surprisingly, in the present case, the appellant has consciously decided not to challenge the award dated 21/01/2022 passed by IVth District Judge,
Shivpuri on the ground of lack of jurisdiction in spite of the fact that this Court had repeatedly pointed out the decisions taken by this Court in similar cases.

10. Be that whatever it may be.
11.
One thing is clear that appellant does not wish to challenge the findings recorded by IVth District Judge, Shivpuri.

The party by maintaining silence cannot confer a jurisdiction on a Court, therefore,
although, appellant may not be interested in challenging the jurisdiction of IVth District Judge,
Shivpuri, but still as already held by this Court in the case of Sanjay Kumar & Ors.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31813 5 AA-220-2023 (supra) IVth District Judge,
Shivpuri had no jurisdiction.

12. So far as the question of condonation is concerned, it is not the case of appellant that after impugned award dated 21/01/2022 was passed by IVth District Judge, Shivpuri, he even approached Divisional Commissioner, Gwalior cum Arbitrator.

The record of Arbitration Tribunal was called and from the order- sheet, it appears that after Commissioner, Gwalior Division, Gwalior received the file back from the Court of IVth District Judge, Shivpuri, he on his own initiated the proceedings without there being any application by appellant and in view of the amendment introduced by which the Collectors of their respective districts were made Arbitrator, Commissioner,

sentences.text: Gwalior Division, Gwalior forwarded the matter to Collector, Shivpuri and Collector, Shivpuri in his turn by order dated 24/03/2023 has dismissed the arbitration.

13. Both these orders i.e. order dated 09/02/2022 passed by Commissioner, Gwalior Division,
Gwalior and order dated 24/03/2023 passed by Collector cum Arbitrator, District Shivpuri have not been challenged.

14. Whether, Commissioner could have forwarded the matter to Collector, Shivpuri in respect of the acquisition which took place in the year 2012 without any remand from the Court of IVth District Judge, Shivpuri or not is also the question which has cropped up but in absence of any challenge,
this Court does not find it necessary to adjudicate the same.

entities.text: Court of IVth District Judge, Shivpuri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Since appellant did not initiate any proceedings before Commissioner or Collector, therefore, it cannot be said that he was bonafidely prosecuting his cause before a forum having no jurisdiction.
15. Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that even otherwise, this appeal is barred by time, accordingly, I.A.No.3554/2023 is hereby rejected.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:31813 6 AA-220-2023 16.
The delay in filing this appeal is hereby rejected and accordingly, this appeal is hereby dismissed as barred by time .

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE PjS/-
